name: STILL
logline: After the funeral, a family opens the shoebox of photographs. Each one you pick up comes alive — a memory you stand inside. The people we love never really leave; they just stop moving. Tonight, they don't have to.

family.grandma: Marion — the one the photos are about. Never still, in any of them.
family.daughter: Ellen — her daughter, fifties. Warm, wry, does most of the talking.
family.grandson: Sam — fourteen, trying not to feel, failing.
family.granddaughter: Maya — nine, asking the questions nobody wants to answer.

frame.prompt: A living room the evening after a funeral, warm lamplight. A woman in her fifties in a dark cardigan sits on a worn sofa beside a low coffee table with an open shoebox of old photographs; a fourteen-year-old boy and a nine-year-old girl lean over the box. Behind her the house is full of relatives: an aunt with a teacup tray, an uncle in a dark suit by the kitchen doorway, coats piled on a chair.
frame.narration: Will you look at this. A whole shoebox of her photographs — she kept every single one. Sam, Maya — come sit. Go on, pick one up. I want to see it again.

memories.label: in the shoebox — the lake picnic, 1986
memories.hint: the year dad set fire to the barbecue
memories.photo_prompt: A faded late-1980s family photograph, slightly overexposed with warm film grain. A lakeside picnic on a checkered blanket: a grandfather in a ridiculous wide-brimmed hat laughing at a smoking portable barbecue, a grandmother mid-laugh holding a paper plate, two children chasing each other by the water. Kodak colors, slight motion blur, developed-print texture with a white border.
memories.alive_prompt: A lakeside picnic on a summer afternoon. A woman of forty in a sundress sits on a checkered blanket beside a tall man in a wide-brim straw hat, a small smoking barbecue and a plate of sausages between them, a jug of lemonade on the blanket. Two children play at the water's edge, tall grass along the shore.
memories.voice: The hat. He wore that hat for twenty years. Mom said the sausages tasted like charcoal smoke until Y2K.
memories.in_world: Listen — you can still hear the water. I always thought the wind would take that hat off him one day.
memories.return_label: put it back in the box
memories.return_line: God, I'd forgotten the hat. Go on — there's more in there.

memories.label: in the shoebox — the training wheels, 2022
memories.photo_prompt: A recent photograph with a phone-camera look, bright summer light. A suburban sidewalk in summer: a grandmother runs bent over behind a small bicycle, one hand on the seat, a helmeted child pedals hard with a determined face, motion blur in her running legs. Developed-print texture, white border, sun flare.
memories.alive_prompt: A quiet suburban street in low golden light. A small girl in a bike helmet rides a small blue bicycle along the sidewalk, a silver-haired woman in her seventies a few steps behind with her hands half-raised. Parked cars line the curb, a dog lies on a porch, lawns on either side.
memories.hud: W / S — pedal. she's right behind you
memories.voice: She let go. That was the whole trick, Maya — she just let go, and then you screamed so loud the neighbors came out.
memories.in_world: That was the summer she decided you were ready. Go on — ride.
memories.return_label: put it back in the box
memories.return_line: She let go on purpose, I swear it. Go on, take another.

memories.label: in the shoebox — the kitchen, every December
memories.photo_prompt: A faded 1990s family photograph, warm indoor flash look with film grain. A cozy kitchen at Christmas: a grandmother with flour on her hands and one cheek mock-scowling, a young daughter laughing behind her with an icing bag, cookie trays and flour dust everywhere, tinsel and a small radio on the counter. Developed-print texture, white border.
memories.alive_prompt: A warm kitchen at Christmas. A woman of forty with flour on one cheek stands at the counter over rolled cookie dough, a tray of cookies and an icing bag beside her, a small radio on the counter, tinsel along the shelf. A teenage girl stands behind her with one hand on a cookie tin. A kettle sits on the stove.
memories.hud: W / S — move around the kitchen
memories.voice: Three hundred cookies a year. Every year. She gave the recipe to no one. Sam, check the tin — I hid one from her in the car.
memories.in_world: Smell that? Three hundred cookies, Maya. The whole street got some.
memories.return_label: put it back in the box
memories.return_line: I can still smell it from here. Keep going — what else did she keep?

memories.label: above the piano — the lake at dawn, 1978
memories.photo_prompt: An old 1970s photograph, faded with age, orange-shifted colors and grain. Misty dawn on a lake: a young man and a young woman in denim sit close on a wooden dock sharing one fishing rod, the girl laughing, mist on the water behind them. Vintage developed print, slight yellowing, white border.
memories.alive_prompt: A wooden dock on a still lake at dawn, mist over the water turning gold. A young woman in denim sits close beside a young man in denim, one fishing rod across their knees, a tackle box at their feet. Reeds along the shore, a loon far out on the water.
memories.hud: W / S — the dock is yours
memories.voice: Before any of us. One rod between the two of them, and I swear neither one ever wanted a fish.
memories.in_world: That's them. Look how still the water is.
memories.return_label: put it back on the wall
memories.return_line: And she kept that one up there all those years.

memories.label: on the bookshelf — everyone, last November
memories.hint: the rare photo where everyone is looking
memories.photo_prompt: A recent photograph from last Thanksgiving, phone-camera look but printed. Three generations crowded around a dinner table: an elderly grandmother at the centre mid-laugh, her daughter beside her, a teenage boy and a small girl leaning in, everyone miraculously looking at the camera at once, candles and turkey and chaos. Warm indoor light, developed-print texture, white border.
memories.alive_prompt: A candlelit Thanksgiving dinner table. An elderly grandmother with a silver bob sits at the centre mid-laugh, a glass raised in one hand, the small girl beside her leaning into her arm. A woman in her fifties and a teenage boy sit across the table, plates and candles and a turkey between them.
memories.hud: W / S — move around the table
memories.voice: Nobody knows who got us all to look at the same time. Look at her. She knew. Somehow she always knew it was the last one.
memories.in_world: All of us here, everyone looking — even Sam. She wanted you to see this one.
memories.return_label: put it down — it's the last one
memories.return_line: She's still here. As long as we keep looking.

staging.reveal_prompt: A living room in warm evening lamplight. A woman in her fifties in a dark cardigan sits on a sofa beside a coffee table with a closed shoebox. A large faded photograph of a misty lake hangs on the wall above the piano, a small framed family photograph stands on the bookshelf. A fourteen-year-old boy and a nine-year-old girl sit on the rug looking around at the walls.
staging.reveal_narration: Well… that's the box empty. But look where she is — everywhere. That one above the piano is her and Dad, summer of '78. And there's all of us on the bookshelf, last November. Go on, look.

ending.title: STILL
ending.subtitle: The people we love never really leave. They just stop moving. Tonight, they didn't have to.
ending.prompt: A living room late at night, one low golden lamp. Old photographs lie in careful rows across the coffee table beside a closed shoebox and two teacups. A large lake photograph hangs above the piano, a small family frame stands on the bookshelf.
ending.voice: She's still here. As long as we keep looking.

ellen.instructions: A woman in her fifties, the day after her mother's funeral, in a house full of relatives. Warm, a little hoarse, gently wry — she laughs mid-sentence once and keeps going. Calling her kids close to the table, speaking over the soft murmur of the gathering. Intimate, close-mic, never performative. Grief is under the words, not in them.

sam.instructions: A fourteen-year-old boy trying to sound casual about his grandmother. Quiet, brief, half-swallowed warmth. One sentence at a time.

maya.instructions: A nine-year-old girl, curious and bright, in a quiet room. Quick, light, innocent questions.

music: soft solo piano, slow, sentimental, licensed CC — fades under voices
